CVE-2026-115932.title: Path traversal in post media lets any registered user read server files
CVE-2026-115932.description:
When a post is published, Postiz treats a media path that is not a web address as a file on the server's disk, but it does not check that the file lies inside the upload directory. A registered user can store a crafted media path with a post, get it past the checks that normally restrict it, and have the publishing worker read an arbitrary file and send it as an attachment to a Discord server the user controls.

The same unconfined reads can be reached through two further routes. One tells the caller whether a file exists and can exhaust the backend's memory, the other delivers the file the same way as the main route. Self-registration is open by default, so the attacker needs no existing account.

CVE-2026-119446.title: Session fixation in the CLI login flow allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain a user's API token
CVE-2026-119446.description:
Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/<token> returns it to whoever started the login.

The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.5.0…

CVE-2026-130159.title: RepoManager: Authenticated Path Traversal allows arbitrary file read via service unit log viewer
CVE-2026-130159.description: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, the authenticated get-unit-log action accepts a caller-controlled logfile value. CVE-2026-98888.title: arm64: kprobes: Allow reentering kprobes while single-stepping
CVE-2026-98888.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

arm64: kprobes: Allow reentering kprobes while single-stepping

A kprobe can be hit while another kprobe is in KPROBE_HIT_SS state. This
can happen when tracing or perf code runs from the debug exception path
while the first kprobe is preparing or executing its out-of-line
single-step instruction.

Currently arm64 treats a kprobe hit in KPROBE_HIT_SS as unrecoverable,
the same as a hit in KPROBE_REENTER. This is too strict. A hit in
KPROBE_HIT_SS is still a one-level reentry and can be handled by saving
the current kprobe state and setting up single-step for the new probe,
just like reentry from KPROBE_HIT_ACTIVE or KPROBE_HIT_SSDONE.

The truly unrecoverable case is hitting another kprobe while already in
KPROBE_REENTER, because the reentry save area has already been consumed.

Move KPROBE_HIT_SS to the recoverable reentry cases and leave
KPROBE_REENTER as the unrecoverable nested reentry case.

CVE-2026-99069.title: Input: ati_remote2 - fix type confusion in device attribute handlers
CVE-2026-99069.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Input: ati_remote2 - fix type confusion in device attribute handlers

Previously, the channel_mask and mode_mask attributes were registered on
the parent usb_device via sysfs_create_group(). When commit b20d6bf8014b
("Input: ati-remote2 - use driver core to instantiate device
attributes") converted the driver to let the driver core manage them via
dev_groups in struct usb_driver, the attributes moved to the bound
usb_interface devices, but the show and store callbacks were not updated
accordingly.

As a result, the callbacks still invoked to_usb_device() on a device
pointer belonging to a struct usb_interface, producing an invalid
usb_device pointer.

Use to_usb_interface() directly in the attribute handlers to obtain the
interface and its driver data.

CVE-2026-99375.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost

When a client loses a byte-range lock, because its lease expired and it
may not recover the lock (nfs.recover_lost_locks=0) or because reclaim
failed, it marks the lock state NFS_LOCK_LOST and fails further I/O by
that lock owner. Otherwise an application that believes it holds a
lock over a range is never told that the lock is gone, and can
overwrite data that another client has since written under its own
lock on that range.

The NFSv4 READ/WRITE and file layout I/O paths apply this in
rpc_call_prepare, where nfs4_set_rw_stateid() returns -EIO for a lost
lock. The flexfiles data server I/O path does not: the NFSv3 data
server path never checked, and the check on the NFSv4 path was removed
when the data server stateid began to be taken from the layout.
